clue.text: Purchase requiring pound always

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from the Latin libra
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: A purchase that demands a pound every single time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchase' looks like buying, but here it means grip or leverage, which is what a lever gives you.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchase in its mechanical sense is a firm hold giving leverage, and a bar used to pry supplies exactly that.

clue.text: Lie about, decidedly laid-back

indicators.note: about means turned around or moved round, so the preceding word is rearranged

parts.note: surely and decidedly both mean certainly

explanation.surface: Someone lazing around, very relaxed indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges LIE to LEI.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something unhurriedly means being relaxed and easy-going, i.e. laid-back.

clue.text: Call on half a dozen to take their seats

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
to sit is to take one's seat

explanation.surface: Dropping in on six people as they sit down.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay a call on someone is to go and see them.

clue.text: Change the positioning back, given latitude

parts.note: rear means back, as in the rear of a building
latitude means scope or freedom, i.e. range

explanation.surface: Moving things backwards because there is room to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is a link; 'back' looks like part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To put things in a different order or layout is to alter their positioning.

clue.text: Perfectly happy to study in temporary accommodation

parts.note: to con is an old verb meaning to study or learn by heart
tented describes people housed in tents, a temporary shelter

explanation.surface: Someone delighted to be revising while camping out.
explanation.definitionFit: Being content means satisfied, wanting nothing more, which is to be perfectly happy.

clue.text: Go riding around on wind system

indicators.note: around says the cycling word goes round the next piece, holding it inside

parts.note: to cycle is to go riding on a bike

explanation.surface: Biking about in a windstorm.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating storm of low pressure, a circulating weather system of winds.

clue.text: An uplifting fragrance now in production

indicators.note: in a down clue, uplifting means a word is read bottom to top, i.e. backwards

parts.note: a scent is a fragrance

explanation.surface: A cheering new perfume being made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' turns AN upward to NA in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something just coming into being is in the early stages of being formed.

clue.text: Spirit needed as some meet hostility

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Morale is needed when facing aggression.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Spirit needed' as definition; 'needed' does not define, so the definition is 'Spirit' and 'needed as' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: The characteristic spirit of a group or era is its guiding character and values.

clue.text: Strange Argentine fruit

indicators.note: strange means odd or altered, so the next word's letters appear in a changed order

explanation.surface: An odd South American fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small orange citrus fruit, a kind of mandarin.

clue.text: Negotiated, having put one's cards on the table

definitions.text: having put one's cards on the table
definitions.meaning: distributed the cards to players in a game

explanation.surface: Struck a bargain after laying the cards out.
explanation.definitionFit: It means traded or did business, and also distributed playing cards to players.

clue.text: Occasions incessant exchange of letters

indicators.note: an exchange of letters here means the letters of the previous word swap places among themselves

explanation.surface: Times when people kept writing to each other non-stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchange of letters' reads as correspondence, but it tells you to rearrange INCESSANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Instances are particular cases or times something happens, that is, occasions.

clue.text: Bird with back an unnaturally reddish colour

parts.note: a hen is a female bird, especially a chicken

indicators.note: with back says the following word is turned round and read backwards

explanation.surface: A bird whose back is an odd shade of red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with back' is the reversal signal on the short word after it; 'unnaturally' belongs to the definition, since the shade comes from a dye.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a plant dye giving hair an artificial red-brown tint, hence a reddish colour not found naturally.

clue.text: Extreme, so to speak

definitions.meaning: the verb meaning to say or give voice to

explanation.surface: Something extreme, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so' just links the two senses; 'so to speak' looks like a fixed phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means complete or absolute; as a verb it means to say aloud or voice words.

clue.text: Review proves ten were not economical

indicators.note: to review is to look over again, so the letters of the next two words are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: An audit shows ten people spent too freely.
explanation.definitionFit: To have overspent is to have paid out more than one should, so they were not thrifty.

clue.text: Cost to be met out of cash, as stated

indicators.note: as stated says the phrase should be heard when spoken rather than read

parts.note: ex means out of, and pence is cash, giving 'ex pence'

explanation.surface: A bill that must be paid out of ready money, as the rules say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be met' is a link describing the cost; 'ex pence' spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlay is something you pay for, so a cost and an expense are the same thing.

clue.text: This has little connection with the mainland

definitions.text: This has little connection with the mainland

parts.words: This has little connection with the mainland
parts.note: sounds like something remote, but describes land joined to the main part only by a narrow neck

explanation.surface: Something largely cut off from the rest of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little connection' means a small link, not hardly any relationship: the land is joined by a thin strip.
explanation.definitionFit: Land almost surrounded by water but attached to a larger mass by a narrow stretch.

clue.text: Inclined to see tournament action

definitions.meaning: jousting with lances at a medieval tourney

explanation.surface: Keen to watch some jousting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to see' links the two senses; 'Inclined' looks like 'keen' but means leaning over.
explanation.definitionFit: It means leaning at an angle, and also charging with a lance at a medieval joust.

clue.text: Guides settle with foreign money

parts.note: to land is to come down and settle, as a bird does
marks were the currency of Germany

explanation.surface: Tour guides putting down roots with euros' predecessors.
explanation.definitionFit: Features that are easy to see act as reference points that help travellers find their way.

clue.text: Raging, in a frenzy about the association

indicators.note: about here means going around the next word, holding it inside
being in a frenzy means wild and disordered, so the word before is scrambled

explanation.surface: Furious, frantic, regarding the club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raging' looks like the definition's mood, but it is the anagram fodder for 'in a frenzy'; 'about' is a container signal, not 'concerning'.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting of people, or the group so assembled, is a coming together in company.

clue.text: Look for no return from American people

indicators.note: return says the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: to look for is to seek
nay is an old word for no

explanation.surface: Don't expect anything back from Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' acts on both pieces together, so the whole two-word run is read backwards rather than each piece alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Yankees is an informal term for people from the United States.

clue.text: Petition — very proper

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so kind'
licit means lawful or proper

explanation.surface: An entirely legitimate appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask for or seek something earnestly is to make a request or plea.

clue.text: Union caught over an apparently sure thing

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
on can mean over, as in 'a lid on the pot'
a cert is a certainty, a horse tipped as a sure winner

explanation.surface: A marriage that seemed a certainty gets caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: CERT, short for certainty, is British racing slang for a horse expected to win; 'apparently' hints it might not.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in concert means acting together, so it is agreement or union.

clue.text: Official organiser of stiff examinations

parts.note: reads like a tough exam board, but 'stiff' is slang for a corpse, and the examinations are inquests into deaths

explanation.surface: The person who sets the hardest exams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stiff' is slang for a dead body, so the 'examinations' are inquests.
explanation.definitionFit: This officer holds inquests into deaths that are sudden or suspicious.

clue.text: He covers up, once discovered in clear violation

indicators.note: once being discovered in another word means it is found sitting inside it
a violation breaks something, so the letters of the word beside it are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A man hiding things, once found breaking the rules openly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' looks like 'formerly' but is fodder; 'violation' is the anagram signal and 'discovered in' places one piece inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A concealer is one who hides things, i.e. someone who keeps them secret.

clue.text: Take care of top artist's source of oil

parts.note: c/o, written CO, is the address abbreviation for care of
PRA is the President of the Royal Academy, Britain's leading art institution

explanation.surface: Looking after a famous painter's oil supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take' is a link. PRA means President of the Royal Academy, the senior painter in that London institution.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried coconut kernel, pressed to extract coconut oil.

clue.text: Overdeveloped a city in Portugal

indicators.note: developed means worked into a new form, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Portuguese city that has grown too much.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed word 'Overdeveloped' must be split: its first part is fodder and 'developed' is the anagram signal. Evora is a city in the Alentejo.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a historic walled town in the Alentejo region, south-central Portugal.

clue.text: A man collecting money for wood

indicators.note: collecting means taking something in, so one word holds another inside it

parts.note: a man is a male
P is penny, a small British coin

explanation.surface: A man going round with a hat for timber.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a tree whose hard timber is used in furniture, a familiar kind of wood.

clue.text: River god of icy regions

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
a lar is a Roman household god

explanation.surface: A river deity from the frozen north.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the areas around the earth's poles, which are frozen.

clue.text: Underworld boss was an animated character

definitions.meaning: the Roman god ruling the land of the dead
a cartoon dog created by Disney

explanation.surface: A gangland chief used to be a cartoon figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was an' links. The Roman god of the dead shares his name with Disney's cartoon dog; 'Underworld boss' suggests a gangster.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruler of Hades in Roman myth, and Mickey Mouse's dog in Disney cartoons.

clue.text: Women who are well used to low scores

definitions.text: Women who are well used to low scores

parts.words: Women who are well used to low scores
parts.note: reads like players getting poor marks, but describes female singers whose musical parts sit in the lowest register

explanation.surface: Women resigned to poor results.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the lowest female singing voices, so they habitually sing low-pitched written parts.

clue.text: Smooth white material, the result of a laboratory bloomer

parts.note: a bloomer is something that blooms, here the flower aster

explanation.surface: White stone produced by a lab blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder (British slang for a mistake) but means a flower. 'the result of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fine-grained translucent stone, typically white, used for carving ornaments.

clue.text: Direction prudish person gives youngster

parts.note: S is south, a compass direction
a prig is a self-righteous, prudish person

explanation.surface: A strait-laced adult giving orders to a child.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an old, informal word for a young person, a scion or offshoot of the family.
